events.title: Spanish deportation of the Caquetío
hints: A 1499 expedition labelled this island and two neighbours worthless for mining.
Many of its Caquetío residents were taken to Hispaniola as forced labour in 1515.
Spain lost the island to a Dutch fleet in 1634.
events.summary: Spanish expeditions reached the island in 1499. Many Caquetío inhabitants were deported as forced labour to Hispaniola from 1515, and the island was used for ranching. A Dutch West India Company fleet captured it in 1634.

events.title: Dutch slave depot and salt pans
hints: A trading company took the island in 1634 and made its deep harbour a hub.
It became a major depot where enslaved Africans were held and resold across the Caribbean and the Spanish Main.
Slavery in this Dutch colony was abolished in 1863.
events.summary: The Dutch West India Company took Curaçao in 1634. Its harbour became a major centre for the trade in enslaved Africans, who were held there and resold to plantations around the Caribbean. Slavery was abolished in 1863.

events.title: British occupation
hints: In December 1807 a British frigate squadron seized the island's harbour in a surprise attack.
It served as a base for British trade with the Spanish Main.
It was returned to the Netherlands in 1816.
events.summary: British naval forces captured the island in December 1807 during the Napoleonic Wars. They used its harbour as a trading and naval base and returned it to the Netherlands in 1816 after the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814.
